source.title: SafeTune: A Unified Faithful Library for Auditing and Repairing Safety Drift in Fine-Tuned LLMs
source.authors: Pratinav Seth; Saisab Sadhu; Anshul Kaushal; Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

record.tranche_reason: The paper directly applies refusal-direction ablation and measures harmful-request refusal on a new model, though only in a small quickstart demonstration.
record.gate_note: The quickstart reports a refusal-direction ablation result. The stated direction location and hidden dimension are not separate outcome rows. Other weight-recovery and safety-drift results do not test the claim versions about a single residual-stream direction.
record.test_reason: A library paper whose quickstart ablates a located refusal direction in Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and reports refusal on held-out harmful prompts. This bears directly on V1's ablation claim in a new model. The extraction procedure is not stated, so the method's match to the original is unverified, and the test has only 4 prompts. All other results concern weight-space recovery or fine-tuning drift, not the direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct for the quickstart: the authors call it a diagnostic counterfactual showing localization, not a safety repair. The paper's overall conclusion is different. Benign fine-tuning drift varies by model and domain, and intervention choice depends on access and calibration. SafeTune is offered as a shared substrate for comparing interventions, not as evidence about the refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: It uses refusal-direction ablation at layer 14 through an inference-time hook. The direction extraction procedure is not specified for this demonstration; all-layer-and-position ablation, addition, and capability preservation are not tested.
record.method_sensitivity: Only layer 14 is reported; no comparison across layers or other settings is given.
record.problems: The direction-ablation demonstration covers one model and four harmful prompts. It reports no harmless-prompt addition test or general-capability evaluation, and does not specify how the direction was extracted for this run.

untested.parts: Direction addition inducing refusal on harmless prompts. Preservation of other abilities. Confirmation that the direction is a harmful-minus-harmless difference in means. Any scale beyond 4 prompts and one 0.5B model.
No weight-edit (abliteration) result; the ablation is a reversible hook with no weights edited.
Not tested. Fine-tuning drift is measured only as refusal rate, not via the direction.

record.verdict_notes: The only direction-related result is the captured terminal output in Figure 3, a library demo. Section 2.1 cites prior work saying refusal-direction degradation tracks safety loss after fine-tuning; this is a cited claim, not a result here. In the finance case study, 'steering' amplified fair-lending refusals (Table 6), but the steering method is not identified as refusal-direction addition and the measure is domain-specific, so it is not linked to V1.

versions.untested_parts: Only harmful-prompt refusal after ablation is tested. The paper does not establish that the direction was computed by the specified harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means method, removed at every layer and position, or that adding it induces refusals to harmless requests. Other abilities are not evaluated.
No released-model weight edit that removes refusal through abliteration is evaluated.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision is tested.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is reported.
No test of how refusal-training choices determine whether a removable direction exists is reported.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the located refusal direction live using a reversible forward hook.
rows.note: The captured quickstart output reports refusal on all four prompts before ablation and none afterward. The harmful response is withheld from the listing.
rows.check: Condition 'layer: 14' overstates what is reported. The text says the direction was extracted at layer 14 (hidden dim 896). It does not say which layers or positions the forward hook ablates. The condition should read 'direction extracted at layer 14; ablated layers/positions not stated'. The value 4/4 to 0/4 and the state are correct.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct; 4 held-out harmful probe prompts; inference-time hook ablating a direction located at layer 14
relationships.reason: Refusal drops from 4/4 at baseline to 0/4 after ablation (r1). The sample is tiny and no capability check is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Refusal fell from 4/4 at baseline to 0/4 after ablation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
